report.summary: Both failures are the same 5-second timeout on the first page.goto('/books') in the logged_in_page fixture, before any assertion about app behavior runs. The other UI tests that use the same fixture and navigation passed in this run, so this looks intermittent rather than a consistent product or test defect. First, check whether the BUGS env var (slow_list) or CI machine load was active for this run, then rerun the ui suite to see if the timeouts reproduce.

causes.title: Intermittent 5s timeout navigating to /books in the logged-in UI fixture
causes.explanation: Both tests fail inside the shared logged_in_page fixture at the first navigation to /books, with Playwright's 5000 ms default timeout (set in tests/ui/conftest.py). The failing step is the first request, before any test-specific behavior. Other tests that use the same fixture and open /books (test_added_book_is_listed, test_book_created_through_api_shows_in_ui, test_deleted_book_disappears) passed, so the page is not consistently broken. The most likely explanation is timing: the /books response sometimes takes longer than 5 s. The app's slow_list seeded bug (app/main.py:160-161) adds a random 0-8 s sleep to list_books, which render_books calls for every /books request (app/main.py:270). That would make these tests flaky, which is not a product_bug. It is only active if BUGS contains slow_list, and the CI workflow does not set BUGS, so either it was set in this environment or the delay comes from CPU contention on the runner (pytest runs with -n auto, so several uvicorn servers and browsers share one machine). The failure logs do not show response timing, so the root cause is not confirmed. Also, the tracebacks point to a Windows path (C:\Users\IvanPosavec\...), while the workflow runs on ubuntu-latest, so this may be a local run rather than the CI job.
evidence: tests.ui.test_books_ui::test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input[chromium] — playwright._impl._errors.TimeoutError: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:59814/books", waiting until "load"
tests.ui.test_login_ui::test_log_out_ends_the_session[chromium] — Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:59812/books", waiting until "load"
tests/ui/conftest.py:5-7: autouse fail_fast fixture calls page.set_default_timeout(5000)
tests/ui/conftest.py:10-15: logged_in_page sets the session cookie and returns the page without any wait for the server
app/main.py:159-161: list_books sleeps random.uniform(0, 8) when 'slow_list' is in BUGS
app/main.py:270: render_books calls list_books(user["id"]) on every /books render
.github/workflows/tests.yml:31-35: CI installs chromium and runs `pytest -m ui -n auto` with no BUGS variable set
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:19-25 and 28-35: other tests using logged_in_page and BooksPage.open() are not in the failed list
causes.suggested_fix: Check the runner environment for a BUGS=slow_list setting and for CPU load under -n auto. Then rerun the ui job a few times. If the timeouts recur, capture the trace (already retained by --tracing=retain-on-failure) and check the response time of /books. Options: lower xdist parallelism for the ui suite, or give page.goto an explicit longer timeout in BooksPage.open() / the fixture. Waiting for a specific element is more reliable than waiting for the 'load' event. Do not just raise the global timeout without first finding out why /books sometimes takes more than 5 s.
